name: Panel Workspace
description: Renders deterministic terminal panel layouts, focus, child-terminal navigation, directional keyboard movement, resize, split, drag, and close behavior.

states: Split the active terminal into multiple panels and inspect headers, inactive masks, separators, and menu actions.
Create and select a child terminal, then inspect the return, title, close, and child-strip presentation.
Drag a primary panel header across directional targets and inspect reversible projection and cancellation.
Split four Panels into a nested layout, then move the active Panel with Shift plus the directional-focus chord and inspect exact leaf exchange without topology or terminal-identity changes.
Split the active terminal, press Command+R, then use W, N, T, S, Control-modified steps, and R reset in keyboard resize mode.

useWhen: A Workbench terminal tab needs the reviewed multi-panel model and its complete interaction projection.
Panel identity, focus, layout, terminal children, resize, drag, split, and close must remain coordinated.
avoidWhen: The layout is generic resizable application chrome with no terminal or Workbench panel semantics.
The caller only needs a low-level resizable primitive or one standalone terminal viewport.
invariants: Every tab retains at least one Panel and exactly one focused Panel resolves inside that tab.
Dragging changes only reversible projection state until a valid directional drop commits the move.
Directional keyboard movement swaps complete neighboring Panel leaves while preserving split topology, weights, slot identities, terminal identities, and focus on the moved source Panel.
Keyboard resize mode captures one exact Tab and Panel, mutates the nearest matching split axis, preserves a visible branch floor, and closes when its target becomes stale.
Closing running or provisioning logical terminals requires localized confirmation before mutation.
Managed close retains topology until every exact presentation close completes; partial failure remains retryable without rollback.
Host PTY and process lifecycle remain outside the Panel workspace owner.
